subject: maths
chapter_title: Vector Algebra: Scalar and Vector Quantities

concepts.title: Scalars, Vectors and Position Vectors
concepts.definition: A scalar carries only a numerical size while a vector carries both a size and a direction; the vector drawn from the origin to a point P is the position vector of P, whose directed segments represent the displacement.
concepts.formula: position vector of P(x, y, z) = x*i_hat + y*j_hat + z*k_hat
concepts.key_idea: Magnitude alone means scalar; magnitude plus direction means vector.
question_patterns: classify the given measure as a scalar or a vector
identify which quantity carries direction as well as magnitude
write the position vector of the point with the given coordinates
represent a displacement as a directed line segment
explain the difference between a scalar and a vector quantity
state the position vector of P with respect to the origin

solution_steps.action: Ask whether a direction is needed alongside the number
solution_steps.explain: Only size means scalar; size with direction means vector.

solution_steps.action: Read the coordinates of the point for its position vector
solution_steps.explain: The coefficients of i hat, j hat and k hat are the coordinates.

solution_steps.action: Draw the arrow from the origin to represent it
solution_steps.explain: The directed segment from O to P pictures the position vector.

concepts.title: Magnitude of a Position Vector
concepts.definition: The length of a vector with components x, y and z comes from the three-dimensional Pythagoras rule: square each component, add the squares, and take the square root.
concepts.key_idea: Three squarings, one sum, one square root give the vector's length.
question_patterns: find the magnitude of the vector with the given components
compute the length of the position vector of the point
evaluate the modulus of the vector x i hat plus y j hat plus z k hat
how long is the arrow represented by the given triple
calculate the size of the vector using the distance formula from the origin
determine the absolute value of the given vector

solution_steps.action: Square and add the three components
solution_steps.explain: The squared length is x squared plus y squared plus z squared.

solution_steps.action: Take the square root of the squared sum
solution_steps.explain: The square root converts squared length into length.

concepts.title: Types of Vectors
concepts.definition: Special vector classes matter in computation: the zero vector has no direction, a unit vector has length one, equal vectors share components, collinear vectors run along parallel lines, and coinitial vectors start from a common point.
concepts.formula: unit vector = vector divided by its own magnitude
concepts.key_idea: Length one, same components, or same line decide the vector's type.
question_patterns: classify the given vectors as equal, collinear or coinitial
explain what makes a vector a unit vector
identify the zero vector among the listed vectors
check whether two given vectors are collinear

solution_steps.action: Compare components for equality or collinearity
solution_steps.explain: Equal vectors match component by component; collinear ones are scalar multiples.

solution_steps.action: Compute the magnitude when length matters
solution_steps.explain: Length one marks a unit vector; zero length marks the zero vector.

solution_steps.action: State the type with the matching criterion
solution_steps.explain: Quote the property that decided the classification.

concepts.title: Addition of Vectors by Triangle and Parallelogram Laws
concepts.definition: Vectors add head to tail: placing the start of one arrow at the tip of another, the sum runs from the free start to the free tip; equivalently, equal initial points make the diagonal of the parallelogram the sum.
concepts.key_idea: Add matching components; the laws only picture the same operation.
question_patterns: find the sum of the two given vectors
add the vectors using the triangle law
apply the parallelogram law to combine the vectors
verify that vector addition is commutative for the given pair
compute the resultant displacement of two successive moves
combine the vectors by adding their i, j and k parts

solution_steps.action: Place the vectors head to tail or from a common point
solution_steps.explain: Both layouts realise the same addition.

solution_steps.action: Add component-wise
solution_steps.explain: First with first, second with second, third with third.

solution_steps.action: Read the sum as the closing side or the diagonal
solution_steps.explain: Triangle law gives the closing side; parallelogram law gives the diagonal.

concepts.title: Components of a Vector Along the Coordinate Axes
concepts.definition: Every space vector splits into three perpendicular pieces, its scalar components multiplying the unit vectors along the axes; the components locate the vector completely and make arithmetic with vectors ordinary number work.
concepts.formula: vector a = a1*i_hat + a2*j_hat + a3*k_hat with scalar components a1, a2, a3
concepts.key_idea: The triple of scalar components is the vector's working identity.
question_patterns: write the given vector in terms of the unit vectors along the axes
find the scalar components of the vector
express the arrow as a combination of i hat, j hat and k hat
identify the components of the vector joining the origin to the point
determine the x, y and z parts of the given vector
decompose the vector along the three coordinate directions

solution_steps.action: Match each axis unit vector with its coefficient
solution_steps.explain: The coefficients are the scalar components.

solution_steps.action: Rebuild the vector from its components when reversing
solution_steps.explain: Multiply each unit vector by its component and add.

solution_steps.action: Use components for later vector arithmetic
solution_steps.explain: Addition, scaling and products all act on components.

concepts.title: Vector Joining Two Points
concepts.definition: The directed segment from point P to point Q has components equal to the coordinate differences: subtract the coordinates of the starting point from those of the ending point, component by component.
concepts.key_idea: Terminal minus initial gives the joining vector's components.
question_patterns: find the vector joining the two given points
determine the directed segment from P to Q in component form
subtract the coordinates to obtain the vector between the points
write the vector from the first point to the second point
which differences give the components of the joining vector
express PQ as a combination of the unit vectors along the axes

solution_steps.action: Name the initial and terminal points
solution_steps.explain: Direction matters: Q minus P, never the reverse.

solution_steps.action: Subtract coordinates terminal minus initial
solution_steps.explain: Each component is the corresponding coordinate difference.

solution_steps.action: Assemble the differences into the component form
solution_steps.explain: The triple of differences is the joining vector.

concepts.title: Distance Between Two Points via Vector Length
concepts.definition: The distance between two points is the magnitude of the joining vector: square the three coordinate differences, add them, and take the square root.
concepts.key_idea: The joining vector's length is the distance between the points.
question_patterns: find the distance between the two given points using vectors
compute how far apart P and Q are
evaluate the magnitude of the vector joining the points
calculate the separation of the two points in space
obtain the length of the segment PQ
determine the distance with the coordinate differences

solution_steps.action: Difference the coordinates component-wise
solution_steps.explain: The joining vector has components terminal minus initial.

solution_steps.action: Difference the remaining coordinates
solution_steps.explain: Collect the y and z differences the same way.

solution_steps.action: Square and add the three differences
solution_steps.explain: The squared length is the sum of the squared differences.

solution_steps.action: Square root the squared total
solution_steps.explain: This is the distance between the two points.

concepts.title: Section Formula for the Division of a Segment
concepts.definition: A point dividing the segment between position vectors p and q in the ratio m to n has position vector the weighted mix of p and q; external division uses the same weights with a sign change, and equal weights give the midpoint.
concepts.formula: position vector of R = (n*p + m*q)/(m + n) for internal division in the ratio m:n
concepts.key_idea: Weighted averaging of the endpoints realises any division ratio.
question_patterns: find the position vector of the point dividing the segment in the given ratio
apply the section formula to the two position vectors
locate the midpoint of the segment using equal weights
divide the line segment externally in the given ratio
determine the coordinates of the point that cuts PQ in ratio m to n

solution_steps.action: Decide whether the division is internal or external
solution_steps.explain: Internal keeps both weights positive; external flips one sign.

solution_steps.action: Form the weighted combination of the endpoint vectors
solution_steps.explain: Multiply each endpoint by the opposite ratio number and add.

solution_steps.action: Divide by the sum of the weights
solution_steps.explain: The result is the position vector of the dividing point.

concepts.title: Scalar Product and Perpendicularity
concepts.definition: The dot product multiplies two vectors into one number: the product of their lengths times the cosine of the angle between them; a zero dot product for nonzero vectors signals a right angle, and a vector dotted with itself gives its squared length.
concepts.formula: dot product = a1*b1 + a2*b2 + a3*b3 which equals magnitude_a * magnitude_b * cos(theta)
concepts.key_idea: One number encodes both the angle and the sizes of the two vectors.
question_patterns: find the dot product of the two given vectors
compute the scalar product in component form
show that the vectors are perpendicular using the dot product
evaluate a dot a and relate it to the squared magnitude
check whether the angle between the vectors is a right angle
decide if the pair of vectors is orthogonal by their scalar product

solution_steps.action: Multiply matching components and add
solution_steps.explain: First times first plus second times second plus third times third.

solution_steps.action: Interpret the sign of the result
solution_steps.explain: Zero means perpendicular, positive acute, negative obtuse.

solution_steps.action: Use the product form for angle reasoning
solution_steps.explain: Dividing by the magnitudes turns the dot product into the cosine.

concepts.title: Cosine of the Angle Between Two Vectors
concepts.definition: The cosine of the angle between two vectors equals their dot product divided by the product of their magnitudes; every ingredient is component arithmetic.
concepts.key_idea: Dot product over the product of lengths is the angle's cosine.
question_patterns: find the cosine of the angle between the two vectors
compute the angle's cosine from the dot product and the magnitudes
evaluate cos of theta for the given pair of vectors
determine the value that the angle formula gives for the two vectors
calculate the ratio of the dot product to the product of the lengths
find how tilted the two vectors are using their scalar product

solution_steps.action: Dot the component triples
solution_steps.explain: Matching components multiply and add.

solution_steps.action: Magnitude of the first vector
solution_steps.explain: Square, add, square root the a-components.

solution_steps.action: Magnitude of the second vector
solution_steps.explain: Same rule for the b-components.

solution_steps.action: Divide the dot product by the magnitude product
solution_steps.explain: The quotient is the cosine of the angle between the vectors.

concepts.title: Projection of a Vector on Another Vector
concepts.definition: The scalar projection of one vector on another is the dot product divided by the length of the vector being projected onto; it measures the shadow length the first vector casts along the second's direction.
concepts.formula: projection of a on b = dot_ab / mag_b
concepts.key_idea: Dot with the target, then divide by the target's length.
question_patterns: find the projection of the vector a on the vector b
compute the shadow of one vector along the other
evaluate the scalar projection using the dot product and the length

solution_steps.action: Dot the two component triples
solution_steps.explain: Matching components multiply and add.

solution_steps.action: Length of the target vector
solution_steps.explain: The b-vector's magnitude uses its three components.

solution_steps.action: Divide the dot product by the target length
solution_steps.explain: This quotient is the scalar projection of a on b.

concepts.title: Cross Product and Vectors Perpendicular to Both
concepts.definition: The vector product of two vectors is a new vector whose length is the product of the lengths times the sine of the included angle and whose direction obeys the right-handed rule; it vanishes exactly when the inputs are parallel, and its direction supplies vectors perpendicular to both inputs.
concepts.formula: cross product magnitude = mag_a * mag_b * sin(theta)
concepts.key_idea: Zero cross product means parallel; its direction is perpendicular to both inputs.
question_patterns: find the cross product of the two given vectors
compute the vector product in determinant form
obtain a unit vector perpendicular to both given vectors

solution_steps.action: Expand the determinant with i hat, j hat, k hat
solution_steps.explain: Each component is a two-by-two minor difference.

solution_steps.action: Check the result for parallelism when needed
solution_steps.explain: A zero cross product certifies parallel inputs.

solution_steps.action: Normalise the cross product for a perpendicular unit vector
solution_steps.explain: Dividing by its magnitude gives the unit normal to both inputs.

concepts.title: Areas of a Parallelogram and a Triangle via the Cross Product
concepts.definition: Adjacent side vectors spanning a parallelogram give its area as the magnitude of their cross product; the triangle on the same adjacent sides takes exactly half that number.
concepts.formula: area of the parallelogram = magnitude of the cross product of the adjacent sides
concepts.key_idea: Cross, then take length: that is the parallelogram area; halve it for the triangle.
question_patterns: find the area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are the given vectors
compute the triangle area from three position vectors using the cross product
evaluate the magnitude of the vector product to get the area
determine the area spanned by the two adjacent side vectors
calculate how much surface the parallelogram covers with vector methods
halve the cross product magnitude for the area of the triangle

solution_steps.action: Cross product x-component
solution_steps.explain: a2*b3 minus a3*b2.

solution_steps.action: Cross product y-component
solution_steps.explain: a3*b1 minus a1*b3.

solution_steps.action: Cross product z-component
solution_steps.explain: a1*b2 minus a2*b1.

solution_steps.action: Square and add the cross components
solution_steps.explain: This is the squared cross product length.

solution_steps.action: Square root for the parallelogram area
solution_steps.explain: The cross product's magnitude equals the parallelogram's area.
